items.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: I went down to Eddie Bell and told him gee, I’d better pick

ctx.x: So Woody Herman was the first big band that you had played with, of that size?

Well no, I was with Jerry Wald, I was with, Abe Lyman, I was with Carl Hoff from the west coast, he hired me. And at that time I had to go and brush up on my reading because in Carl Hoff’s band, the violin player was the arranger. There was only one violin, but he wrote double stops for the guitar and double stops for the violin so it would sort of sound like — that’s the book when I come in — and they couldn’t get any guitar player to read it. So I come closer to it, but I went down to Eddie Bell and told him…

up on my reading. So Eddie Bell says go and see Alan Reuss. But Alan was sick and he was going to go out to California. So I just went over two times with Alan. He says aah, keep doing what you’re doing, it’s all right. No, but that was lucky that I was taught how to read a little bit, on the banjo. See that’s what I try to tell these guys. This month, I think it’s May, April, May, I think it’s May, Jazz Guitar, there’s a magazine called just Jazz Guitar, they just sent me a proof of one of my solos I had…
